grape downy mildew.cause: Water mold (Plasmopara viticola), a fungus-like organism
grape downy mildew.symptoms: Pale yellow, oily-looking spots on the upper side of leaves. After a warm, humid night a white downy growth appears on the underside of the spot. Old spots turn brown and angular. Young shoots, tendrils, flowers and young berries can be covered with white down, then turn brown, shrivel and fall.
look_alikes: Powdery mildew (powdery white dust, not oily spots)
Grape leaf blister mite (white felt inside blister-like bumps)
Nutrient disorders or frost damage on leaves
grape downy mildew.favourable_weather: Warm, wet weather and humid nights during active vine growth, with rain splash and leaves that stay wet. It can spread within days.

weather_profile.note: Warm wet weather and humid nights. No verified numbers loaded yet. Add them from NRCG Pune.

organic_control: Remove and destroy badly infected leaves, shoots and bunches
Open up the canopy by pruning and training so leaves dry quickly
Avoid overhead irrigation and keep the area under the vines free of weeds
To confirm it, put a spotted leaf in a plastic bag with a damp paper overnight. White down on the underside points to downy mildew
grape downy mildew.chemical_control: Use only a product that is registered in India for grape and this disease. Protection before infection matters, so ask your agriculture officer or NRCG advisories for the product, dose and spray schedule. No product or dose is given here.
prevention: Manage the canopy so air and light reach the leaves and bunches
Keep drainage good and avoid long periods of leaf wetness
Follow the NRCG or your state spray calendar for your area
Scout after warm, wet nights, especially at the young shoot and flowering stages
grape downy mildew.when_to_call_expert: If oil spots or white down appear on flowers, young bunches or many leaves, because crop loss can be heavy if it is not controlled in time.

grape powdery mildew.symptoms: White to grey powdery patches on the upper or lower side of leaves, on shoots and on berries. Young berries can be coated white, and later they may crack or look rough and russeted. Leaves can become distorted, and heavily infected bunches lose quality.
look_alikes: Downy mildew (oily yellow spots with white down underneath)
Spray residue such as sulphur or lime
The natural pale waxy bloom on healthy berries
grape powdery mildew.favourable_weather: Moderate temperatures and humid air with shaded, dense canopies. Unlike many diseases it does not need free water on the leaf.

weather_profile.note: Moderate temperatures (roughly 20 to 30 C). Free water is not required. Add exact figures from NRCG Pune.

organic_control: Remove and destroy badly affected shoots and bunches
Open up the canopy by pruning and shoot positioning so sun and air reach the bunches
Avoid excess nitrogen that produces dense, soft growth
Ask your KVK or NRCG about non-chemical options used in your area
grape powdery mildew.chemical_control: Use only a product that is registered in India for grape and this disease. Disease pressure is season-long, so ask your agriculture officer or NRCG advisories for the product, dose and spray schedule. No product or dose is given here.
prevention: Choose vineyard sites and training systems with good air movement
Keep the canopy open through the season
Scout from early shoot growth, especially on bunches after flowering
Follow the NRCG or state spray calendar for your area
grape powdery mildew.when_to_call_expert: If white coating appears on young bunches or berries, because fruit quality can be lost quickly.

grape botrytis bunch rot.symptoms: Berries soften, turn brown or purplish and rot, and a grey fuzzy mould grows on them in humid conditions. Rot spreads from berry to berry inside tight bunches and can ruin the whole bunch before or after harvest.
look_alikes: Other bunch or berry rots such as black rot or sour rot
Normal colour change as berries ripen
Sunburn or heat damage on berries
Splitting of berries after heavy rain
grape botrytis bunch rot.favourable_weather: Humid, damp weather with dense canopies and tightly packed bunches. Rain near ripening and injuries to berries help it.

weather_profile.note: Humid, cool to moderate and damp conditions. Hot, dry weather makes it less likely. No verified numbers loaded yet.

organic_control: Remove and destroy rotten berries and bunches, away from the vineyard
Open up the canopy and remove leaves around bunches so they dry quickly
Avoid wounding berries and control pests and birds that damage them
Harvest promptly and sort out rotten berries before packing
grape botrytis bunch rot.chemical_control: Use only a product that is registered in India for grape and this disease. Ask your agriculture officer or NRCG advisories for the product, dose and timing. No product or dose is given here.
prevention: Use training and pruning that keep bunches loose and well ventilated
Avoid too much nitrogen, which makes soft, dense growth
Avoid irrigation or sprinklers that wet the bunches near harvest
Check and sort bunches during storage and transport
grape botrytis bunch rot.when_to_call_expert: If grey mould is spreading across bunches, or if you are not sure whether the rot is Botrytis or another bunch rot, because treatment depends on the exact rot.
